# Read the preprocessed billboard dataset from the RDS file
top_songs <- read_rds("top_songs.rds")

# Build the trajectory plot and assign it to billboard_plot
billboard_plot <- ggplot(top_songs, aes(x = week, y = rank, color = track)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 1.5) +
  scale_y_reverse(limits = c(100, 1)) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Billboard Rank Trajectory of Longevity Hits (2000)",
    subtitle = "Songs that spent 45 or more weeks on the Hot 100",
    x = "Week on the Chart",
    y = "Rank (1 is the top rank)",
    color = "Song Title"
  )

# Save the plot as a PNG image file
ggsave("billboard_plot.png", plot = billboard_plot)

ℹ Use the conflicted package (<http://conflicted.r-lib.org/>) to force all conflicts to become errors

# Pivot the billboard data from wide to long, convert week numbers to integers,
# filter for songs on the chart for at least 45 weeks, and assign the result to top_songs
top_songs <- billboard |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("wk"),
    names_to = "week",
    names_prefix = "wk",
    values_to = "rank",
    values_drop_na = TRUE
  ) |>
  mutate(week = as.integer(week)) |>
  group_by(artist, track) |>
  filter(n() >= 45) |>
  ungroup()

# Save the dataset to an RDS file
write_rds(top_songs, "top_songs.rds")

write_rds(top_songs, file = “clean_data.rds”)
